notes: Hand-labelled retrieval eval for the recommendation agent. Run it as a unit
test on every prompt, model, or ranking-weight change — without it, every
tuning decision after P2 is blind.
rejectIds matters as much as expectIds. It catches the failure this whole
design is built to avoid: an event whose wording attracts a query it cannot
serve. Cases tagged 'adversarial' exist only for that — see opera-venue-trap,
where four unrelated events sit at Sydney Opera House and would all match the
word 'opera' on venue name alone.
IDs are real rows in ticket_db as of corpusSnapshot. Duplicate events are in
the corpus on purpose (the same show seeded several times); where duplicates
exist, all of them are listed in expectIds, because dedupe is an ingest-time
job and this file measures retrieval, not presentation.
expectRelaxation: true means the correct behaviour is to find nothing inside
the stated constraint and widen it in the fixed order (price, then time
window, then exclude — never city). Scoring such a case as a miss would push
the ranker to over-return, so score it on whether relaxation fired and what
it surfaced afterwards.
Today for date-relative queries is corpusSnapshot. Most of the corpus sits in
2027, so 'this weekend' legitimately returns almost nothing.

dim-*    cau hoi nham vao tung dim, ke ca ba dim KHONG co vector

chi luu dang chu thi chuyen gi xay ra.

Cac ca temporal duoc cham voi 'hom nay' = corpusSnapshot. Nhan cua chung tu muc nat khi ngay that troi qua: temporal-next-month tung liet ke thang 9 trong khi thang sau cua snapshot la thang 10, va cham 0% cho mot cau tra loi dung. Doi corpusSnapshot thi phai tinh lai expectIds cua moi ca co truong 'rule' nhac den mot thang cu the.

cases.why: Artist names resolve through full-text on primaryArtist^2.5, never through the vector. A distilled facet vector has no reason to encode a proper noun.
Includes the Hanoi row that has no venue or category set — a proper-noun hit must not depend on metadata completeness.
Two seeded variants of the same tour.
Typed without diacritics, as a Vietnamese user on a plain keyboard would. Must still reach the accented row.
Same diacritic case. 'my' is also a common English word, so this doubles as a check that a short stopword-like token does not blow up the match.
fuzziness=AUTO gives two edits at this length. Typo tolerance belongs to the full-text path; the vector path must not be asked to rescue it.
Sơn Tùng is VPOP, not KPOP. Adjacent genres are exactly where a loose vector match goes wrong.
Metallica must not surface for an electronic query despite both being loud, high-energy, large-scale.
Ballet and musical share the THEATER category. The genre facet has to do the separating.
Inverse of genre-ballet. Note the corpus names the ballets '— The Musical', so the title text actively misleads here; genre must win over name.
TEDx is CONFERENCE but genre IDEAS — acceptable either way, so it is in neither list.

cases.query: something calm and relaxing, nothing intense
cases.why: The core atmosphere test. 'nothing intense' is a negation and must reach exclude, not the vector — embedded, it sits next to 'intense'.
Mirror of vibe-calm. If both queries return the same set, the atmosphere dim is carrying no signal at all.

cases.query: something to take the kids to
cases.why: UFC and a late-night electronic set are the two clearest wrong answers for a family query.
Scale should come from the capacity_band attribute, derived from ticket count — not guessed from adjectives in the description.

cases.query: concert with an amazing light show
cases.why: Coldplay's LED wristbands and Daft Punk's pyramid stage are stated in the descriptions, so this is a genuine distillation test rather than a genre proxy.

cases.query: somewhere i can learn something and meet people
cases.why: No category word in the query. Purely a participation and audience match.

cases.query: a legendary rivalry match with history behind it
cases.why: F1 and the All-Star Game are sport but not rivalry fixtures. The descriptions carry the distinction explicitly.

cases.query: a timeless classic story on stage
a show where both nights have different setlists
cases.why: Highly specific fact stated only in Metallica's description. If this misses, distillation is dropping detail that only lives in the long copy.
Tests the participation dim, which is text-only and not embedded — expected to rank on format plus atmosphere alone.

cases.query: a concert but not too crowded
cases.why: The whole corpus is arena and stadium scale, so the honest answer is that nothing qualifies. Scored on whether exclude=large-scale fired and relaxation reported what it widened — not on what came back.
Canonical negation trap. Embedded, 'nothing electronic' lands next to 'electronic' and returns exactly the rejects.
Doubly hard: the ballets are titled '— The Musical' in this corpus, so the negation has to beat the event name.
Category-level exclusion. expectIds is a sample, not exhaustive — score recall on rejects.

cases.query: something in london, not a conference
cases.why: Hard city filter and a category exclusion in one turn. Neither belongs in the vector.
No vibe at all. Turn-1 behaviour: maximise diversity of format across the five returned, do not return five Formula 1 rows.
Wimbledon Finals @ Paris is in the city but is not a concert.
Vietnamese query against English event content. City resolution must handle the accented form; the vibe half is empty so ranking falls back to popularity plus diversity.
'new york' must be consumed as a city filter and stripped from the vector. Left in, it matches any description that merely mentions the city.
City in SQL, mood in the vector. Metallica is in London and must lose on atmosphere alone.
Unaccented 'hanoi' must resolve to the accented city value stored in the row.
Both codes share genre=FOOTBALL, so an unqualified query legitimately returns both. See american-football and soccer for the split.
Four unrelated events sit at Sydney Opera House, so 'opera' matches them on venueName^1.5. A developer conference must never be the top hit for 'opera'. The single most informative case in this file.
genre=FOOTBALL covers two different sports in this corpus. The tag filter cannot separate them; only the format facet can.
Inverse of american-football. The word 'soccer' appears in neither description, so this rides entirely on the format facet.
Venue is a proper noun and a hard filter, never a vector term. Six unrelated formats share this venue — returning all of them is correct, and diversity should decide the top five.

cases.query: somewhere to unwind after a long week
cases.why: The phrasing from the spec's own example of marketing copy that misleads. 'Unwind' is filler; the real signal is a low-intensity atmosphere, and the answer must not be a stadium metal show.
'Reunion' appears in both event names. Cheap to get right through full-text, and a canary that the name field is still being searched at all.
This row has null venue, category and genre. It must stay reachable by name even though it will carry almost no facets — the ranker must not require a facet score to return anything.
Relative to corpusSnapshot the nearest events are Super Bowl Tokyo on 10–11 Sep. Correct behaviour is to widen the time window and say so, never to answer with a bare question.

Nhan phu thuoc ngay thang thi tu muc nat. Ca nay tung cham 0% trong khi he thong tra ve dung thang 10 — that bai nam o nhan, khong o he thong. Bat cu ai doi corpusSnapshot deu phai tinh lai expectIds cua no.
cases.rule: thang 10/2026 — thang sau corpusSnapshot 2026-09-06. Nhan cu liet ke thang 9, tuc doc 'next month' la '30 ngay toi'; no duoc viet khi hom nay con o thang 8 va mau thuan voi chinh quy uoc cua file nay.

cases.why: A bare month name with no year resolves to the next occurrence — February 2027, not a past February.

No slots at all. Must still return five events, chosen to maximise format diversity rather than score — one concert, one sport, one theatre, one conference, one other. Scored on the spread of category across the five, not on membership.

cases.query: i'm bored, what should i do
cases.why: Same rule as turn1-bare-greeting. The point of turn 1 is to harvest a click, which is cheaper than asking a question.
